Yes, Sepo can do this, but it does **not** currently have a post-merge CI check in the orchestrator chain.

Current behavior:
- `/orchestrate` keeps a bounded handoff chain only for explicitly orchestrated runs: [README.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/README.md#L64-L65), [README.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/README.md#L83-L83).
- After `fix-pr` succeeds, the chain dispatches `review`, not a CI watcher: [.agent/src/handoff.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L460-L474).
- The `fix-pr` workflow only hands back while the PR is still open: [.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L300-L318).
- Self-merge checks PR status checks before merging or enables GitHub auto-merge while checks are pending: [.agent/src/self-merge.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/self-merge.ts#L280-L321).
- Once `agent-self-merge` reports `merged`, the orchestrator stops: [.agent/src/handoff.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L539-L540).
- Existing merged-PR workflows cover memory, rubrics, and agent branch cleanup, not post-merge CI monitoring: [.github/workflows/agent-branch-cleanup.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-branch-cleanup.yml#L3-L20).

Implementation approach I’d recommend:

1. Add a deterministic post-merge CI status route, probably `agent-post-merge-ci.yml`, triggered by `pull_request_target.closed` where `merged == true`.
2. Gate it narrowly so it only runs for Sepo-relevant merges, for example PRs with a Sepo self-merge marker, fix-pr status marker, orchestrator marker, or trusted `agent/*` head branch.
3. Add typed helpers under `.agent/src` to resolve the merged PR’s merge commit/default-branch head and inspect check runs/statuses with `checks: read` and `statuses: read`.
4. Treat pending CI as a bounded wait/poll, not an orchestrator LLM step. If checks are pending, wait a short configured window; if still pending, post “pending” with run links and stop.
5. If post-merge CI fails, post a visible status comment on the merged PR and optionally dispatch a new orchestrated follow-up issue or implementation route, depending on the policy we want.
6. Add tests around status summarization, event gating, and comment formatting.
7. Update the orchestrator docs to say pre-merge self-merge checks are already enforced, and post-merge CI is handled by the new merged-PR workflow.

Clarification before coding: should a post-merge CI failure only **report** on the merged PR, or should Sepo also create/dispatch a follow-up fix automatically?

Yes, that easier path is reasonable **for an opportunistic CI check**, but I would not describe it as “watch CI after merge.”

What a prompt-only change can do:
- Tell the orchestrator planner to inspect current PR/check status after a successful `fix-pr`.
- If CI is already failing or clearly pending, it can choose `blocked`/`stop` with a visible message instead of immediately handing off to `review`.
- If CI is green, it can continue with the existing allowed `fix-pr -> review` path.

What it cannot do by itself:
- Add a new `ci-status` action. The prompt schema only allows `implement | review | fix-pr | agent-self-approve | agent-self-merge`: [.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L71-L83).
- Override runtime policy. The prompt explicitly says runtime validates the planner decision: [.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md#L20-L40).
- Keep watching after the PR is merged. `agent-fix-pr.yml` only dispatches the orchestrator while the PR is still open: [.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L300-L318).
- Change the allowed post-`fix-pr` handoff. Runtime currently allows successful `fix-pr` to hand off to `review`, and rejects other handoff actions through the policy path: [.agent/src/handoff.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L658-L670).

Suggested small implementation:
1. Update `.github/prompts/agent-orchestrator.md` to say: after successful `fix-pr`, inspect current PR CI/check status when available before choosing the next step.
2. Instruct it to:
   - hand off to `review` when fixes succeeded and checks are green or unavailable;
   - choose `blocked`/`stop` with `user_message` when checks are failing;
   - optionally choose `blocked`/`stop` when checks are still pending and another automatic review would be premature.
3. Update `.agent/docs/architecture/agent-orchestrator.md` to document this as “opportunistic CI inspection,” not durable post-merge monitoring.
4. Add/adjust prompt tests only if there is existing coverage for orchestrator prompt content or planner policy expectations.

So: prompt-only is a good first pass for “check CI before continuing.” For true “watch CI after merge,” we still need a merged-PR or workflow-run based workflow.

Because a direct `fix-pr -> fix-pr` loop is not currently an allowed orchestrator transition.

Right now, after `fix-pr` succeeds, runtime policy only allows the chain to hand back to `review`: [.agent/src/handoff.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L460-L474). The planner can choose `stop`/`blocked`, but if it tries to dispatch another `fix-pr`, runtime validation rejects it because the allowed next action is `review`: [.agent/src/handoff.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L658-L670).

So the better prompt-only behavior is probably:

- If CI is **pending**, wait/check briefly if practical; otherwise block with “CI still pending.”
- If CI is **green**, hand off to `review`.
- If CI is **failing and actionable**, still hand off to `review`, because review is the existing policy gate that can synthesize the CI failure into a concrete `FIX_PR` recommendation.
- If CI is **failing but flaky/environmental/unclear**, block or stop with a visible message.

That preserves the current loop shape:

`fix-pr -> review -> fix-pr`

instead of adding a new direct loop:

`fix-pr -> fix-pr -> fix-pr`

The direct loop may be useful later, but it needs runtime support: a new allowed transition, stricter round limits, failure classification, and clear handoff context so the agent does not keep pushing speculative fixes for flaky CI or infra failures.

https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/363#discussion_r3321191195

I mean it seems the inline review can look at the CI messages?  @sepo-agent

Yes, I think you’re right. The referenced comment is exactly the better shape: the review pass can read CI output, turn it into a concrete inline finding, and then let the existing review -> fix-pr path handle it.

That is better than having the orchestrator itself block on failing CI.

Current pieces already line up:

- Review synthesis can inspect current PR state and must verify unresolved findings against current artifacts/current PR state: [.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L9-L18).
- It can post inline comments for concrete line-specific issues: [.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L28-L41).
- It emits `Recommended Next Step: FIX_PR` when unresolved findings are safe for automation: [.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review-synthesize.md#L110-L117).
- The review workflow hands that synthesis back to the orchestrator: [.github/workflows/agent-review.yml](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L379-L402).
- The orchestrator already maps review findings back to `fix-pr`: [.agent/src/handoff.ts](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/handoff.ts#L503-L511).
- `fix-pr` already prioritizes latest review synthesis/action items: [.github/prompts/agent-fix-pr.md](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-fix-pr.md#L22-L30).

So I’d revise the earlier plan:

1. After successful `fix-pr`, keep handing off to `review`.
2. Strengthen the review synthesis prompt to explicitly inspect failing CI/check output when available.
3. Tell review synthesis to convert actionable CI failures into normal findings, including inline comments when tied to a changed line.
4. Let `Recommended Next Step: FIX_PR` drive the next automated fix pass.

That preserves the existing safe loop:

`fix-pr -> review -> fix-pr`

and makes CI failures first-class review findings instead of adding a separate CI watcher route.
Closing because this agent issue has had no activity for 30 days.
